It is used twice in the file (lines 145 and 194), i.e. it is not a step of a single argument.
findings.fix: Drop `private` (and name it for the surface, e.g. `measure_setOf_mem_ray_le_ediam`), or additionally export a `geometricPathLength`-level finiteness lemma `volume {s : ℝ | 0 ≤ s ∧ x + s • v ∈ S} ≠ ⊤` from `Bornology.IsBounded S` and `‖v‖ = 1`.
findings.issue: `volume_setOf_le_ediam` is `private`, but it is stated purely in upstream vocabulary (`volume`, `ediam`, the ray set) and is the only route to `volume {s | 0 ≤ s ∧ x + s • v ∈ S} ≠ ⊤`. Without it, `geometricPathLength_le_diam` (line 143) has no finiteness content — `volume.real` is finite by construction, so the inequality also holds when the parameter set has infinite measure and the value is the junk `0`. The docstring claim at line 141-142 ("In particular it is finite for a medium of compact support") is not backed by any public lemma.

summary: The public surface cannot express the finiteness that §0.2's first theorem claims: the only ENNReal-level bound is `private`, and the ray-integrability extracted inside `densityWeightedPathLength_le` is not exported, so both `_le_diam` and `_le` are satisfiable by junk values. Minor: the nonnegativity and measurability lemmas carry no automation attributes.
